source: real-chart-bench data/verified_pairs (registry.json + ground_truth.json + axis_pixel_candidates.json), commit range up to eb0d255
license_notice: All figures are drawn from open-access papers recorded with license_id "cc-by" in this repo's registry.json / papers.json manifest. That value comes from OpenAlex's `license` field and carries no version number (CC BY 1.0/2.0/3.0/4.0 are all recorded identically). Cite these as "CC BY" without a version unless you independently verify the specific paper's actual license version from the publisher. Do not write "CC BY 4.0" for any of these figures based on this bundle alone.
caveats: License version: license_id is the bare string "cc-by" from OpenAlex, with no version attached. Design doc §7.30's "(CC BY 4.0)" is an inference, not a per-paper verification -- do not upgrade any of these to "CC BY 4.0" without checking the publisher's actual license page for that DOI.

sample_id / samplename do not exist anywhere in this repo's committed data. ground_truth.json curves carry only x, y, prop_x, prop_y, unit_x, unit_y (no per-curve legend/sample label). Starrydata's raw CSV format has a sample_id column (see adapter/starrydata_csv.py's docstring) but it was not preserved through this repo's pairing/verification pipeline. Because there is no reliable curve-index-to-legend mapping in the committed data, series_label is omitted from every curve in this bundle rather than guessed from registry.json's free-text "evidence" field (which does describe curve colors/ordering in prose for some entries, but matching that prose to a specific curve-array index was judged too unreliable to encode as structured data).

printed_axis (x_min_label/x_max_label/y_min_label/y_max_label/x_unit/y_unit) comes from axis_pixel_candidates.json, which is two independent vision-LLM reads cross-checked against each other and, for these 6 entries, additionally owner-reviewed (status=owner_reviewed) -- but it is still not an independent human re-measurement from scratch. Treat pixel positions as strong-but-not-certified ground truth.

x_range/y_range (from registry.json) is sometimes WIDER than printed_axis's min/max label -- this is the normal 'benign_margin' framing margin most chart libraries add around the plotted data (matplotlib/origin default padding), not an error. E.g. paper 27759/fig 25217: x_range=[300,1000] but the printed axis's smallest labeled tick is 400. If back-calculating pixel calibration from x_range/y_range's exact numeric bounds, prefer printed_axis's min/max label (the actual tick values) over x_range/y_range's endpoints where they differ.

All 6 picks passed this repo's automated axis-range classifier (domain/pairing_checks.py::classify_range_disagreement) as benign_margin on both axes, confirming the registry range and the printed axis are in the same unit space -- this was verified per-figure against data/verified_pairs/audit/visual-audit.md, not assumed from metadata alone.
